name: Amoxicillin 500mg
description: A penicillin-type antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections including pneumonia, bronchitis, ear infections, urinary tract infections, and skin infections.
side_effects: Common: diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache, skin rash. Rare: severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis), liver problems, blood disorders.
interactions: Drug interactions: Methotrexate (increased toxicity), Warfarin (increased bleeding risk), oral contraceptives (reduced effectiveness). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. Dairy products do not significantly affect absorption.
contraindications: Allergy to penicillins or cephalosporins. Use with caution in patients with kidney disease, liver disease, or history of antibiotic-associated colitis.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C in a dry place. Keep capsules in original packaging.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 500mg every 8 hours (3 times daily) or 875mg every 12 hours. Take at evenly spaced intervals. Complete the full course even if you feel better.
missed_dose_guidance: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double the dose.

name: Paracetamol 500mg
description: Used to relieve mild to moderate pain (headache, toothache, backache, muscle aches) and reduce fever. Does not reduce inflammation.
side_effects: Common: generally well tolerated at recommended doses. Rare: skin rash, blood disorders, liver damage (especially with overdose or chronic alcohol use).
interactions: Drug interactions: Warfarin (may increase bleeding risk with prolonged use), alcohol (increased liver toxicity), Carbamazepine (increased liver toxicity risk). Food interactions: Avoid excessive alcohol consumption.
contraindications: Severe liver impairment or active liver disease. Use with caution in patients with kidney disease, chronic alcohol use, or malnutrition.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 500mg to 1000mg every 4–6 hours as needed. Maximum 4000mg (4g) per day. Do not exceed recommended dose.
missed_dose_guidance: Since this is taken as needed for pain/fever, a missed dose is not usually a concern. Do not take a double dose.

name: Metformin 500mg
description: First-line medication for type 2 diabetes mellitus. Lowers blood glucose by reducing hepatic glucose production and improving insulin sensitivity.
side_effects: Common: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, loss of appetite, metallic taste. Rare: lactic acidosis (very rare but serious), vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use.
interactions: Drug interactions: Alcohol (increased risk of lactic acidosis), contrast dyes (temporarily stop metformin), Cimetidine (increased metformin levels). Food interactions: Take with meals to reduce GI side effects.
contraindications: Severe kidney impairment (eGFR <30), acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, history of lactic acidosis. Temporarily discontinue before procedures with contrast dye.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from light and moisture.
dosage_schedule: Adults: Start with 500mg once or twice daily with meals. May increase gradually to 2000mg/day. Take with food.
missed_dose_guidance: Take the missed dose with your next meal. If almost time for next dose, skip it. Do not double up. Monitor blood sugar levels.

name: Atorvastatin 10mg
description: Used to lower cholesterol and triglycerides in the blood, reducing the risk of heart attack and stroke. Part of the statin drug family.
side_effects: Common: headache, muscle pain, joint pain, nausea, diarrhea. Rare: rhabdomyolysis (muscle breakdown), liver damage, memory problems.
interactions: Drug interactions: Cyclosporine, Gemfibrozil, Erythromycin (increased statin levels and muscle toxicity risk). Food interactions: Avoid large quantities of grapefruit juice (increases drug levels).
contraindications: Active liver disease, unexplained persistent elevations of liver enzymes, pregnancy, breastfeeding.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 10–20mg once daily. Can be taken at any time of day, with or without food. Taken long-term.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Never double dose.

name: Omeprazole 20mg
description: Reduces stomach acid production. Used to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcers, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
side_effects: Common: headache, nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, flatulence. Rare: vitamin B12 deficiency, magnesium deficiency, bone fractures with long-term use, kidney problems.
interactions: Drug interactions: Clopidogrel (reduced effectiveness — avoid combination), Methotrexate (increased levels), Diazepam (slower metabolism). Food interactions: Take 30 minutes before a meal on an empty stomach.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to omeprazole or other PPIs. Use with caution in patients with liver disease.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C in a dry place. Do not crush or chew capsules.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 20mg once daily, 30 minutes before breakfast. For severe cases, 40mg daily. Course duration depends on condition (4–8 weeks for ulcers).
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses together.

name: Amlodipine 5mg
description: Used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and certain types of angina (chest pain). Works by relaxing blood vessels.
side_effects: Common: swelling of ankles/feet (edema), dizziness, flushing, headache, fatigue. Rare: rapid heartbeat, liver problems, severe skin reactions.
interactions: Drug interactions: Simvastatin (limit simvastatin to 20mg), Cyclosporine (increased cyclosporine levels). Food interactions: Grapefruit may increase drug levels — limit consumption.
contraindications: Severe hypotension (very low blood pressure), severe aortic stenosis, unstable angina, cardiogenic shock.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 5mg once daily. May increase to 10mg if needed. Take at the same time each day. Do not stop suddenly.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If less than 12 hours until next dose, skip it. Never take double dose.

name: Cetirizine 10mg
description: A second-generation antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms including sneezing, runny nose, itchy/watery eyes, and hives (urticaria).
side_effects: Common: drowsiness, dry mouth, headache, fatigue. Rare: palpitations, liver dysfunction, severe allergic reactions.
interactions: Drug interactions: Theophylline (slightly reduced cetirizine clearance), CNS depressants (increased drowsiness). Food interactions: Alcohol may increase drowsiness. Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Severe kidney impairment (dose adjustment required), hypersensitivity to cetirizine or hydroxyzine.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 10mg once daily (or 5mg twice daily). Can be taken morning or evening.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. Skip if close to the next dose. Do not double dose.

name: Azithromycin 500mg
description: A macrolide antibiotic used to treat a wide variety of bacterial infections including respiratory infections, skin infections, ear infections, and sexually transmitted diseases.
side_effects: Common: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache. Rare: liver problems, QT prolongation (heart rhythm changes), hearing loss.
interactions: Drug interactions: Warfarin (increased bleeding risk), Antacids with aluminum/magnesium (take 1 hour before or 2 hours after antacid), Digoxin (increased levels). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. Avoid taking with antacids simultaneously.
contraindications: History of cholestatic jaundice or liver dysfunction with prior azithromycin use. Allergy to macrolide antibiotics. Use with caution in patients with QT prolongation.
storage_instructions: Store below 30°C. Protect from light and moisture.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 500mg on Day 1, then 250mg daily on Days 2–5. OR 500mg daily for 3 days. Take at the same time each day.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If almost time for next dose, skip it. Complete the full prescribed course.

name: Losartan 50mg
description: An angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) used to treat hypertension, diabetic nephropathy, and to reduce stroke risk. Relaxes blood vessels.
side_effects: Common: dizziness, fatigue, nasal congestion, back pain, diarrhea. Rare: hyperkalemia (high potassium), kidney impairment, angioedema.
interactions: Drug interactions: Potassium supplements/potassium-sparing diuretics (risk of hyperkalemia), NSAIDs (reduced antihypertensive effect), Lithium (increased lithium levels). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. Avoid potassium-rich salt substitutes.
contraindications: Pregnancy (can cause fetal harm — stop immediately if pregnant), severe liver impairment, bilateral renal artery stenosis.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 50mg once daily. May increase to 100mg once daily. Take at the same time each day.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double dose.

name: Ibuprofen 400mg
description: A nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to relieve pain, reduce inflammation, and lower fever. Effective for headache, dental pain, menstrual cramps, and arthritis.
side_effects: Common: stomach pain, nausea, heartburn, dizziness, headache. Rare: GI bleeding, kidney problems, cardiovascular events, severe skin reactions.
interactions: Drug interactions: Aspirin (reduced cardioprotective effect), Warfarin (increased bleeding), ACE inhibitors/ARBs (reduced blood pressure control), Lithium (increased levels). Food interactions: Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset. Avoid alcohol.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding or peptic ulcer, severe heart failure, severe kidney or liver disease, third trimester of pregnancy, aspirin-sensitive asthma.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 200–400mg every 4–6 hours as needed. Maximum 1200mg/day (OTC) or 3200mg/day (prescription). Take with food.
missed_dose_guidance: Since often taken as needed, a missed dose is not usually a concern. If on a schedule, take as soon as you remember but do not double up.

name: Ciprofloxacin 500mg
description: A fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat urinary tract infections, respiratory infections, bone/joint infections, and gastrointestinal infections.
side_effects: Common: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, dizziness, headache. Rare: tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, QT prolongation, C. difficile infection.
interactions: Drug interactions: Theophylline (increased levels), Warfarin (increased bleeding risk), Antacids/Iron/Calcium (reduced absorption — take 2 hours apart). Food interactions: AVOID dairy products and calcium-fortified foods within 2 hours of taking. Can be taken with or without other food.
contraindications: History of tendon disorders with fluoroquinolones, myasthenia gravis, allergy to quinolones. Use with extreme caution in elderly patients.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 250–750mg twice daily depending on infection severity. Take at 12-hour intervals. Complete full course.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If almost time for next dose, skip it. Do not double dose. Stay well hydrated.

name: Pantoprazole 40mg
description: A proton pump inhibitor that reduces stomach acid production. Used for GERD, erosive esophagitis, and peptic ulcer disease.
side_effects: Common: headache, diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain. Rare: vitamin B12 and magnesium deficiency, bone fractures, C. difficile infection.
interactions: Drug interactions: Methotrexate (increased levels), Warfarin (monitor INR), Atazanavir (reduced absorption). Food interactions: Take 30–60 minutes before a meal. Swallow whole — do not crush or chew.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to PPIs. Use with caution in patients with liver disease. Not recommended for long-term use without medical supervision.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from moisture. Keep in original packaging.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 40mg once daily before breakfast. Duration: 4–8 weeks for ulcers, may be longer for GERD maintenance.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to the next dose, skip it. Do not take two doses at the same time.

name: Metoprolol 50mg
description: A selective beta-1 blocker used to treat hypertension, angina, heart failure, and to prevent migraine. Reduces heart rate and blood pressure.
side_effects: Common: fatigue, dizziness, cold hands/feet, slow heartbeat, diarrhea, nausea. Rare: bronchospasm, depression, heart failure worsening.
interactions: Drug interactions: Verapamil/Diltiazem (severe bradycardia), Clonidine (rebound hypertension if stopped together), MAO inhibitors (hypertensive crisis). Food interactions: Take with or immediately after food to enhance absorption.
contraindications: Severe bradycardia, heart block (2nd/3rd degree), cardiogenic shock, uncontrolled heart failure, sick sinus syndrome (without pacemaker).
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from moisture. Do not crush extended-release tablets.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 25–100mg once daily for extended-release form. Do not abruptly stop — taper gradually over 1–2 weeks.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If within 8 hours of next dose, skip it. NEVER stop abruptly — risk of rebound hypertension.

name: Levothyroxine 50mcg
description: Synthetic thyroid hormone used to treat hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid). Replaces the hormone normally produced by the thyroid gland.
side_effects: Common (usually from over-dosing): palpitations, sweating, tremor, weight loss, nervousness, headache, diarrhea. Rare: chest pain, osteoporosis with long-term over-dosing.
interactions: Drug interactions: Calcium/Iron supplements (reduced absorption — take 4 hours apart), Warfarin (increased effect), Antacids (reduced absorption). Food interactions: Take on an EMPTY STOMACH, 30–60 minutes BEFORE breakfast. Soy and high-fiber foods may reduce absorption.
contraindications: Untreated adrenal insufficiency, acute myocardial infarction, thyrotoxicosis.
storage_instructions: Store at 25°C. Protect from light and moisture.
dosage_schedule: Adults: typically 50–200mcg once daily in the morning on an empty stomach. Dose adjusted based on TSH levels every 6–8 weeks.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember on the same day. If you miss an entire day, take two tablets the next day. Do not make a habit of doubling doses.

name: Doxycycline 100mg
description: A tetracycline antibiotic used to treat acne, respiratory infections, urinary infections, Lyme disease, malaria prophylaxis, and various sexually transmitted infections.
side_effects: Common: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, photosensitivity (increased sunburn risk), esophageal irritation. Rare: liver toxicity, intracranial hypertension, tooth discoloration in children.
interactions: Drug interactions: Antacids/Iron/Calcium (take 2–3 hours apart), Warfarin (increased bleeding), oral contraceptives (possibly reduced effectiveness), Isotretinoin (increased intracranial pressure risk). Food interactions: AVOID dairy products, calcium, and iron-rich foods within 2 hours. Take with a full glass of water.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, children under 8 years (tooth staining), severe liver disease.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from light. Do not use expired doxycycline — can become toxic.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 100mg twice daily on Day 1, then 100mg once or twice daily. Take with a full glass of water. Do NOT lie down for 30 minutes after taking.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to the next dose, skip it. Complete the full course. Do not double dose.

name: Salbutamol Inhaler 100mcg
description: A short-acting beta-2 agonist inhaler used for quick relief of asthma symptoms and bronchospasm. Opens up the airways in the lungs within minutes.
side_effects: Common: tremor, headache, palpitations, muscle cramps, nervousness. Rare: paradoxical bronchospasm, hypokalemia, severe allergic reactions.
interactions: Drug interactions: Beta-blockers (may reduce effectiveness — avoid non-selective beta-blockers), Diuretics (increased hypokalemia risk), MAO inhibitors (increased cardiovascular effects). Food interactions: No significant food interactions.
contraindications: Use with caution in patients with heart disease, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, hypokalemia.
storage_instructions: Store below 30°C. Do not freeze. Do not puncture or burn canister. Keep away from direct sunlight.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 1–2 puffs every 4–6 hours as needed for symptoms. Shake well before use. Rinse mouth after use.
missed_dose_guidance: Use only when needed for symptoms. If on a regular schedule, take as soon as you remember but do not double the puffs.

name: Clopidogrel 75mg
description: An antiplatelet medication that prevents blood clots. Used after heart attacks, strokes, and in patients with peripheral arterial disease or stent placement.
side_effects: Common: bleeding (bruising easily), diarrhea, stomach pain, indigestion. Rare: severe bleeding, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), liver problems.
interactions: Drug interactions: Omeprazole/Esomeprazole (AVOID — reduces effectiveness), NSAIDs (increased bleeding), Warfarin (increased bleeding risk). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. No specific food restrictions.
contraindications: Active pathological bleeding (peptic ulcer, intracranial hemorrhage), severe liver impairment.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C. No special storage requirements.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 75mg once daily. After acute coronary syndrome, may start with 300mg loading dose then 75mg daily. Take at the same time each day.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not stop taking without consulting your doctor — risk of blood clots.

name: Prednisolone 5mg
description: A corticosteroid used to treat inflammatory and autoimmune conditions including asthma, allergic reactions, rheumatoid arthritis, and inflammatory bowel disease.
side_effects: Common: increased appetite, weight gain, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, indigestion. Long-term: osteoporosis, diabetes, cataracts, adrenal suppression, increased infection risk.
interactions: Drug interactions: NSAIDs (increased GI bleeding risk), Warfarin (variable effect), Diabetes medications (may need dose increase), live vaccines (AVOID). Food interactions: Take with food to reduce stomach upset. Limit salt intake.
contraindications: Systemic fungal infections, live vaccine administration. Use with caution in diabetes, osteoporosis, peptic ulcer, and immunocompromised patients.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from light and moisture.
dosage_schedule: Adults: variable, 5–60mg daily depending on condition. Usually taken in the morning with food. Taper gradually — do NOT stop suddenly.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. NEVER stop corticosteroids suddenly — must taper under medical guidance.

name: Diclofenac 50mg
description: A nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug used for pain relief and inflammation in conditions like arthritis, gout, sprains, dental pain, and post-operative pain.
side_effects: Common: stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, rash. Rare: GI bleeding, cardiovascular events, liver/kidney problems, severe skin reactions.
interactions: Drug interactions: ACE inhibitors/ARBs (reduced effect, kidney risk), Warfarin (increased bleeding), Lithium (increased levels), Methotrexate (increased toxicity). Food interactions: Take with food or after meals. Avoid alcohol.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding, severe heart failure, severe liver/kidney disease, third trimester pregnancy, aspirin allergy.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 50mg 2–3 times daily with food. Maximum 150mg/day. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose.

name: Ranitidine 150mg
description: An H2 blocker that reduces stomach acid production. Used to treat and prevent peptic ulcers, GERD, and conditions of excess stomach acid.
side_effects: Common: headache, dizziness, constipation, diarrhea. Rare: liver problems, blood disorders, confusion in elderly.
interactions: Drug interactions: Ketoconazole/Itraconazole (reduced absorption), Warfarin (slight increase in effect), Procainamide (increased levels). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to ranitidine. Use with caution in kidney or liver disease.
storage_instructions: Store below 30°C. Protect from light and moisture.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 150mg twice daily (morning and bedtime) or 300mg once daily at bedtime. Duration: 4–8 weeks for ulcer healing.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If almost time for next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double dose.

name: Montelukast 10mg
description: Used for prevention and long-term management of asthma and relief of allergic rhinitis. Blocks leukotrienes that cause airway inflammation.
side_effects: Common: headache, stomach pain, heartburn, fatigue. Rare: mood/behavior changes (depression, suicidal thoughts — FDA boxed warning), liver problems, allergic reactions.
interactions: Drug interactions: Phenobarbital (reduced montelukast levels), CYP2C8 inhibitors (increased levels). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity. Use with caution and monitoring for neuropsychiatric symptoms.
storage_instructions: Store at 25°C. Protect from moisture and light.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 10mg once daily in the evening. For asthma + allergic rhinitis, take in the evening. Not for acute asthma attacks.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip the missed dose. Continue the regular schedule.

name: Aspirin 75mg
description: Low-dose aspirin used for cardiovascular protection — prevention of heart attacks and strokes. Also used as a blood thinner after stent placement.
side_effects: Common: stomach irritation, indigestion, nausea, increased bleeding tendency. Rare: GI bleeding, hemorrhagic stroke, tinnitus, Reye's syndrome in children.
interactions: Drug interactions: Warfarin (increased bleeding risk), other NSAIDs/Ibuprofen (may reduce aspirin's cardioprotective effect — take aspirin first), Methotrexate (increased toxicity). Food interactions: Take with food to reduce stomach irritation. Avoid alcohol.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding, hemophilia, children under 16 (Reye's syndrome), severe liver/kidney disease, allergy to NSAIDs.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from moisture. Do not use if tablets smell of vinegar.
dosage_schedule: Cardiovascular prevention: 75mg once daily, preferably in the morning with or after food. Do not crush enteric-coated tablets.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not stop taking without consulting your doctor.

name: Fluconazole 150mg
description: A triazole antifungal used to treat fungal infections including vaginal candidiasis (yeast infections), oral thrush, and systemic fungal infections.
side_effects: Common: headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, rash. Rare: liver damage, QT prolongation, severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome).
interactions: Drug interactions: Warfarin (increased bleeding — monitor INR), Statins (increased risk of muscle damage), Phenytoin (increased levels), oral hypoglycemics (increased hypoglycemia risk). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to fluconazole or other azoles. Concomitant use with terfenadine or cisapride. Severe liver disease.
dosage_schedule: Vaginal candidiasis: Single dose of 150mg. Oral thrush: 200mg on Day 1, then 100mg daily for 7–14 days. Dose varies by infection type.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next scheduled dose, skip the missed one. Complete full course for infections.

name: Gabapentin 300mg
description: Used to treat epilepsy (seizures), neuropathic pain (nerve pain from diabetes, shingles), and restless leg syndrome.
side_effects: Common: drowsiness, dizziness, fatigue, headache, nausea, weight gain, peripheral edema. Rare: suicidal thoughts, respiratory depression (especially with opioids), angioedema.
interactions: Drug interactions: Opioids (increased CNS/respiratory depression), Antacids (reduced absorption — take 2 hours apart), Alcohol (increased drowsiness). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity. Use with caution in kidney disease (dose adjustment needed), respiratory disease, elderly patients.
dosage_schedule: Adults: Start 300mg on Day 1 (evening), 300mg twice daily on Day 2, then 300mg three times daily. May increase up to 3600mg/day. Doses should be evenly spaced (max 12 hours between doses).
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do NOT stop suddenly — taper over at least 1 week to avoid seizures.

name: Cephalexin 500mg
description: A first-generation cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat skin infections, urinary tract infections, respiratory tract infections, bone infections, and otitis media.
side_effects: Common: diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache. Rare: allergic reactions (especially if penicillin-allergic), C. difficile colitis, blood disorders.
interactions: Drug interactions: Probenecid (increased cephalexin levels), Metformin (increased metformin levels), Warfarin (monitor INR). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. Taking with food may reduce stomach upset.
contraindications: Known allergy to cephalosporins. Cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy (~1–10%). Use with caution in kidney disease.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 250–500mg every 6 hours (4 times daily) or 500mg every 12 hours. Typical course: 7–14 days. Complete full course.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to the next dose, skip it. Do not double dose. Complete the antibiotic course.

name: Esomeprazole 40mg
description: A proton pump inhibitor that reduces stomach acid. Used for GERD, erosive esophagitis, and H. pylori eradication (in combination therapy).
side_effects: Common: headache, diarrhea, nausea, flatulence. Rare: C. difficile infection, bone fractures, magnesium deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency.
interactions: Drug interactions: Clopidogrel (AVOID — significantly reduces clopidogrel effectiveness), Methotrexate (increased levels), Warfarin (monitor INR). Food interactions: Take at least 1 hour before meals. Swallow whole.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to PPIs. Avoid co-administration with Clopidogrel.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 20–40mg once daily before breakfast. 40mg for 4–8 weeks for erosive esophagitis. 20mg for maintenance.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose.

name: Sertraline 50mg
description: A selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant used for depression, anxiety, OCD, PTSD, panic disorder, and social anxiety disorder.
side_effects: Common: nausea, diarrhea, insomnia, drowsiness, dry mouth, dizziness, sexual dysfunction. Rare: serotonin syndrome, suicidal thoughts (especially in young adults), bleeding.
interactions: Drug interactions: MAO inhibitors (AVOID — serotonin syndrome, wait 14 days), Warfarin/NSAIDs (increased bleeding), Tramadol (seizure risk), other SSRIs/SNRIs (serotonin syndrome). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. Avoid alcohol.
contraindications: Concurrent or recent MAO inhibitor use (within 14 days), concurrent pimozide use. Use with caution in seizure disorders, liver disease, and bipolar disorder.
dosage_schedule: Adults: Start 50mg once daily (morning or evening). May increase by 50mg/week increments. Maximum 200mg/day. Takes 2–4 weeks for full effect.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do NOT stop suddenly — taper gradually to avoid withdrawal symptoms.

name: Furosemide 40mg
description: A potent loop diuretic (water pill) used to treat fluid retention (edema) in heart failure, liver disease, and kidney disease. Also used for hypertension.
side_effects: Common: increased urination, dehydration, dizziness, headache, muscle cramps. Rare: severe electrolyte imbalance (low potassium, sodium, magnesium), gout, hearing loss (high doses).
interactions: Drug interactions: ACE inhibitors (first-dose hypotension), Digoxin (hypokalemia increases toxicity), Lithium (increased levels), Aminoglycosides (increased ototoxicity). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. Take in the morning to avoid nighttime urination.
contraindications: Anuria (no urine output), severe electrolyte imbalance, hepatic encephalopathy, hypersensitivity to sulfonamides.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from light. Discolored tablets should not be used.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 20–80mg once daily in the morning. May increase in 20mg increments. Take early in the day to avoid nighttime urination.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If it's afternoon/evening, skip it to avoid nighttime urination. Do not double dose.

name: Domperidone 10mg
description: An antiemetic and prokinetic agent used to relieve nausea, vomiting, bloating, and feeling of fullness. Also used for gastroparesis.
side_effects: Common: dry mouth, headache, drowsiness, diarrhea. Rare: QT prolongation, cardiac arrhythmias, increased prolactin (galactorrhea, gynecomastia).
interactions: Drug interactions: QT-prolonging drugs (Erythromycin, Ketoconazole — AVOID), CYP3A4 inhibitors (increased levels), Anticholinergics (reduced domperidone effect). Food interactions: Take 15–30 minutes BEFORE meals.
contraindications: Known cardiac conditions (especially QT prolongation), prolactin-releasing pituitary tumor, GI bleeding/obstruction, concurrent potent CYP3A4 inhibitors.
storage_instructions: Store below 30°C. Protect from light and moisture.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 10mg up to 3 times daily, 15–30 minutes before meals. Maximum 30mg/day. Do not use for more than 7 days without medical advice.
missed_dose_guidance: Take before the next meal. If close to next meal, skip the missed dose. Do not double dose.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide 25mg
description: A thiazide diuretic used to treat hypertension and fluid retention. Often used in combination with other antihypertensive agents.
side_effects: Common: increased urination, dizziness, headache, muscle weakness. Rare: hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hyperglycemia, gout, photosensitivity.
interactions: Drug interactions: Lithium (increased levels), Digoxin (hypokalemia increases toxicity), NSAIDs (reduced diuretic effect), Diabetes medications (may need adjustment). Food interactions: Take in the morning with food. Eat potassium-rich foods (bananas, oranges).
contraindications: Anuria, severe kidney or liver failure, refractory hypokalemia, Addison's disease, sulfonamide allergy.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 12.5–25mg once daily in the morning. Maximum 50mg/day. Take early to avoid nighttime urination.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If afternoon, skip to avoid nighttime urination. Do not double dose.

name: Tramadol 50mg
description: A centrally acting synthetic opioid analgesic used for moderate to moderately severe pain. Works on both opioid receptors and serotonin/norepinephrine reuptake.
side_effects: Common: nausea, dizziness, constipation, headache, drowsiness, sweating. Rare: seizures, serotonin syndrome, respiratory depression, dependence.
interactions: Drug interactions: SSRIs/SNRIs (serotonin syndrome risk), MAO inhibitors (AVOID), Carbamazepine (reduced effect), CNS depressants/alcohol (additive sedation). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. AVOID alcohol entirely.
contraindications: Severe respiratory depression, acute intoxication, concurrent MAO inhibitors, uncontrolled epilepsy. Use with extreme caution in seizure disorders.
storage_instructions: Store below 30°C. Controlled substance — store securely.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 50–100mg every 4–6 hours as needed. Maximum 400mg/day. Start with lowest effective dose.
missed_dose_guidance: If on a schedule, take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not take extra doses. Do not use for longer than prescribed.

name: Lisinopril 10mg
description: An ACE inhibitor used to treat hypertension, heart failure, and to improve survival after heart attack. Also used for diabetic nephropathy.
side_effects: Common: dry cough (persistent), dizziness, headache, fatigue. Rare: angioedema (swelling of face/tongue — seek emergency help), hyperkalemia, kidney impairment.
interactions: Drug interactions: Potassium supplements/K-sparing diuretics (hyperkalemia), NSAIDs (reduced effect + kidney risk), Lithium (increased levels), Aliskiren (AVOID in diabetes). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. Avoid potassium-rich salt substitutes.
contraindications: Pregnancy (causes fetal harm), history of angioedema, bilateral renal artery stenosis, concurrent use with Aliskiren in diabetics.
dosage_schedule: Adults: Start 10mg once daily. Usual range: 10–40mg daily. Take at the same time each day.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose. Do not stop suddenly.

name: Clindamycin 300mg
description: A lincosamide antibiotic used for serious infections including skin, soft tissue, bone, joint, and dental infections. Also used for acne and pelvic inflammatory disease.
side_effects: Common: diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, rash. Rare: C. difficile colitis (potentially fatal — stop if severe diarrhea occurs), liver dysfunction, blood disorders.
interactions: Drug interactions: Erythromycin (antagonistic — avoid combination), neuromuscular blockers (enhanced blockade), Warfarin (increased bleeding risk). Food interactions: Take with a full glass of water. Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: History of C. difficile colitis, known allergy to clindamycin or lincomycin.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 150–450mg every 6 hours depending on severity. Take with a full glass of water to prevent esophageal irritation.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Complete the full course. Do not double dose.

name: Rosuvastatin 10mg
description: A potent statin used to lower LDL cholesterol and triglycerides while raising HDL cholesterol. Reduces cardiovascular risk.
side_effects: Common: headache, muscle pain, nausea, abdominal pain, weakness. Rare: rhabdomyolysis, liver damage, diabetes (slight increased risk), memory problems.
interactions: Drug interactions: Cyclosporine (limit rosuvastatin dose), Gemfibrozil (increased muscle toxicity risk), Warfarin (increased INR — monitor). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. No significant grapefruit interaction (unlike other statins).
contraindications: Active liver disease, unexplained persistent elevations of liver enzymes, pregnancy, breastfeeding.
dosage_schedule: Adults: Start 10mg once daily. Range: 5–40mg daily. Can be taken at any time of day.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose.

name: Loratadine 10mg
description: A non-sedating second-generation antihistamine used to relieve allergic rhinitis, hives (urticaria), and other allergy symptoms.
side_effects: Common: headache, drowsiness (less than first-gen), dry mouth, fatigue. Rare: palpitations, liver dysfunction.
interactions: Drug interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (Ketoconazole, Erythromycin — increased levels but generally well tolerated). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity. Dose adjustment in severe liver disease.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 10mg once daily. Can be taken morning or evening.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose.

name: Warfarin 5mg
description: An oral anticoagulant (blood thinner) used to prevent and treat blood clots in conditions like atrial fibrillation, DVT, pulmonary embolism, and after mechanical heart valve replacement.
side_effects: Common: bleeding (bruising, nosebleeds, prolonged bleeding from cuts), hair loss. Rare: major hemorrhage, skin necrosis, purple toe syndrome.
interactions: Drug interactions: MANY — Antibiotics, NSAIDs, Aspirin, Amiodarone, Fluconazole (increase bleeding risk). Vitamin K intake affects efficacy. Alcohol, Rifampin (decrease effect). ALWAYS inform your doctor of all medications. Food interactions: Maintain CONSISTENT intake of vitamin K-rich foods (green leafy vegetables). Do not make sudden dietary changes.
contraindications: Active major bleeding, pregnancy, hemorrhagic stroke, severe liver disease, uncontrolled hypertension.
dosage_schedule: Adults: Dose individualized based on INR (International Normalized Ratio). Typical: 2–10mg daily. Take at the SAME time each day. Regular INR monitoring required.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember on the same day. If you miss an entire day, DO NOT double the next day's dose. Contact your doctor. Keep a log of missed doses.

name: Levofloxacin 500mg
description: A fluoroquinolone antibiotic used for pneumonia, sinusitis, urinary tract infections, skin infections, and chronic bronchitis exacerbations.
side_effects: Common: nausea, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, insomnia. Rare: tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, QT prolongation, aortic dissection, C. difficile colitis.
interactions: Drug interactions: Antacids/Iron/Calcium/Magnesium (take 2 hours apart), Warfarin (increased bleeding), NSAIDs (increased seizure risk), Theophylline (increased levels). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. Stay well hydrated.
contraindications: History of tendon disorders with fluoroquinolones, myasthenia gravis, epilepsy. Avoid in children under 18.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 250–750mg once daily depending on infection type. Duration: 5–14 days. Take at the same time each day.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Complete the full prescribed course.

name: Spironolactone 25mg
description: A potassium-sparing diuretic used for heart failure, liver cirrhosis (ascites), hypertension, and hyperaldosteronism. Also used off-label for acne and hirsutism.
side_effects: Common: breast tenderness (gynecomastia in men), menstrual irregularities, dizziness, nausea, diarrhea. Rare: hyperkalemia (dangerously high potassium), kidney dysfunction.
interactions: Drug interactions: ACE inhibitors/ARBs (hyperkalemia risk), Potassium supplements (AVOID), NSAIDs (reduced diuretic effect + kidney risk), Digoxin (increased levels). Food interactions: Take with food to improve absorption. AVOID excess potassium-rich foods.
contraindications: Hyperkalemia, Addison's disease, severe kidney impairment, anuria.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 25–100mg daily in 1–2 divided doses. Take with food. May take several weeks for full effect.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose. Monitor potassium levels regularly.

name: Ondansetron 4mg
description: A 5-HT3 receptor antagonist used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and post-surgery.
side_effects: Common: headache, constipation, fatigue, dizziness. Rare: QT prolongation, serotonin syndrome (with serotonergic drugs), liver enzyme elevation.
interactions: Drug interactions: Apomorphine (AVOID — severe hypotension), Tramadol (reduced analgesic effect), SSRIs (serotonin syndrome risk). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Concurrent use with apomorphine. Known QT prolongation. Congenital long QT syndrome.
dosage_schedule: Prevention of nausea: 4–8mg 30 minutes before chemotherapy, then 4mg every 8 hours for 1–2 days. Post-surgical: 4mg before anesthesia or after surgery.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose.

name: Calcium + Vitamin D3 500mg/250IU
description: A calcium and vitamin D supplement used to prevent and treat calcium deficiency, osteoporosis, and to support bone health.
side_effects: Common: constipation, gas, bloating, stomach upset. Rare: hypercalcemia (excessive calcium), kidney stones.
interactions: Drug interactions: Tetracycline/Fluoroquinolone antibiotics (take 2 hours apart — reduces antibiotic absorption), Levothyroxine (take 4 hours apart), Bisphosphonates (take 30 min apart). Food interactions: Best absorbed when taken with food. Avoid taking with high-oxalate foods (spinach, rhubarb) or high-fiber foods.
contraindications: Hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, severe kidney disease, kidney stones, vitamin D toxicity.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 1 tablet twice daily with meals. Total daily calcium should not exceed 2000mg from all sources.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose.

name: Glimepiride 2mg
description: A sulfonylurea oral antidiabetic medication used to treat type 2 diabetes. Stimulates insulin release from the pancreas.
side_effects: Common: hypoglycemia (low blood sugar — tremor, sweating, dizziness, confusion), weight gain, nausea. Rare: blood disorders, liver problems, severe allergic reactions.
interactions: Drug interactions: Beta-blockers (may mask hypoglycemia symptoms), Fluconazole (increased hypoglycemia risk), NSAIDs (increased effect), Alcohol (unpredictable blood sugar effects). Food interactions: Take with breakfast or first main meal of the day.
contraindications: Type 1 diabetes, diabetic ketoacidosis, severe kidney or liver disease, sulfonamide allergy.
dosage_schedule: Adults: Start 1mg once daily with breakfast. May increase to 2–4mg. Maximum 8mg/day. Always take with food.
missed_dose_guidance: Take with the next meal. Do NOT double dose. Monitor blood sugar. If hypoglycemic, consume glucose/sugar immediately.

name: Telmisartan 40mg
description: An angiotensin II receptor blocker used to treat hypertension and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients.
side_effects: Common: dizziness, diarrhea, upper respiratory infection, back pain. Rare: hyperkalemia, angioedema, kidney impairment.
interactions: Drug interactions: Potassium supplements (hyperkalemia), NSAIDs (reduced effect + kidney risk), Lithium (increased levels), Digoxin (increased levels). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Pregnancy, bilateral renal artery stenosis, severe liver disease.
storage_instructions: Store below 30°C. Keep in original packaging. Protect from moisture.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 40mg once daily. May increase to 80mg if needed. Take at the same time each day.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not stop taking without consulting your doctor.

name: Metronidazole 400mg
description: An antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication used to treat anaerobic bacterial infections, dental infections, H. pylori (with other drugs), amoebiasis, and giardiasis.
side_effects: Common: nausea, metallic taste, loss of appetite, headache, dark urine (harmless). Rare: peripheral neuropathy (numbness/tingling), seizures, liver toxicity.
interactions: Drug interactions: Alcohol (SEVERE — disulfiram-like reaction: flushing, vomiting, rapid heartbeat. Avoid during and for 48 hours after), Warfarin (increased bleeding), Lithium (increased toxicity), Phenytoin (altered levels). Food interactions: ABSOLUTELY avoid alcohol. Take with food to reduce nausea.
contraindications: First trimester pregnancy, neurological disorders, severe liver disease. Avoid alcohol.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 400mg 2–3 times daily for 5–7 days depending on infection. Take with or after food. Complete the full course.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose. Complete the full course.

name: Insulin Glargine 100IU/mL
description: A long-acting basal insulin analog used to manage blood sugar in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Provides steady insulin levels over 24 hours.
side_effects: Common: hypoglycemia, weight gain, injection site reactions (redness, swelling, itching). Rare: severe hypoglycemia, lipodystrophy (fat changes at injection sites), allergic reactions.
interactions: Drug interactions: Oral antidiabetics (additive hypoglycemia), Beta-blockers (mask hypoglycemia symptoms), Thiazolidinediones (increased fluid retention), Corticosteroids (increase blood sugar). Food interactions: Consistent carbohydrate intake important. Do not skip meals.
contraindications: During episodes of hypoglycemia, known allergy to insulin glargine.
storage_instructions: Unopened: Store in refrigerator (2–8°C). Do NOT freeze. In-use pen: Store at room temperature (below 30°C) for up to 28 days. Protect from direct heat and light.
dosage_schedule: Adults: Dose individualized. Typical starting: 10 IU once daily at the same time each day (usually bedtime). Adjust based on blood sugar monitoring.
missed_dose_guidance: If you remember within 12 hours, take the dose. If more than 12 hours, take your normal dose at the next scheduled time. Monitor blood sugar closely. Do NOT double dose.

name: Folic Acid 5mg
description: A B-vitamin (B9) supplement used to treat and prevent folate deficiency anemia, and recommended before and during pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects.
side_effects: Common: generally well tolerated. Uncommon: nausea, bloating, flatulence. Rare: allergic reactions, may mask vitamin B12 deficiency.
interactions: Drug interactions: Methotrexate (antagonistic effect — unless used specifically as folate rescue), Phenytoin (mutual reduction), Sulfasalazine (reduced folate absorption). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Untreated vitamin B12 deficiency (folic acid can mask B12 deficiency). Avoid in folate-dependent tumors.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from light and moisture.
dosage_schedule: Folate deficiency: 5mg daily for 4 months. Pregnancy prevention: 400mcg–5mg daily, starting 3 months before conception and continuing through first 12 weeks.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Not critical to double up on a missed dose.

name: Enalapril 5mg
description: An ACE inhibitor used to treat hypertension, heart failure, and to prevent kidney damage in diabetic patients. Works by relaxing blood vessels.
side_effects: Common: dry cough, dizziness, headache, fatigue, nausea. Rare: angioedema, hyperkalemia, kidney impairment, severe hypotension.
interactions: Drug interactions: Potassium supplements/K-sparing diuretics (hyperkalemia), NSAIDs (reduced effect), Lithium (increased levels). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. Avoid potassium-rich salt substitutes.
contraindications: Pregnancy, history of angioedema, bilateral renal artery stenosis.
dosage_schedule: Adults: Start 5mg once daily. Usual range: 5–40mg daily in 1–2 doses. Heart failure: start at 2.5mg.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose.

name: Chlorpheniramine 4mg
description: A first-generation antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms including sneezing, itching, runny nose, and hives. Also used in cold remedies.
side_effects: Common: drowsiness (significant), dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, constipation, urinary retention. Rare: seizures, paradoxical excitation in children.
interactions: Drug interactions: CNS depressants/alcohol (enhanced sedation), MAO inhibitors (prolonged anticholinergic effects), Anticholinergic drugs (additive effects). Food interactions: Avoid alcohol. Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention, severe asthma (during acute attack), newborns/premature infants. Use with caution in elderly.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 4mg every 4–6 hours as needed. Maximum 24mg/day. Causes significant drowsiness — avoid driving.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose.

name: Sitagliptin 100mg
description: A DPP-4 inhibitor used to improve blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes. Works by increasing incretin levels to stimulate insulin release after meals.
side_effects: Common: headache, nasopharyngitis (stuffy nose), upper respiratory infection. Rare: pancreatitis, severe joint pain, bullous pemphigoid (skin blistering).
interactions: Drug interactions: Insulin/Sulfonylureas (increased hypoglycemia risk — may need dose reduction), Digoxin (slightly increased levels). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
contraindications: Type 1 diabetes, diabetic ketoacidosis, history of pancreatitis. Dose adjustment in kidney impairment.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 100mg once daily. Can be taken at any time of day, with or without food.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not take two doses on the same day.

name: Multivitamin + Minerals
strength: Various (Vitamin A, B-complex, C, D, E, Iron, Zinc, etc.)
description: A comprehensive daily multivitamin and mineral supplement to fill nutritional gaps. Contains essential vitamins (A, B1, B2, B6, B12, C, D, E) and minerals (Iron, Zinc, Calcium, Magnesium).
side_effects: Common: nausea, stomach upset, constipation (from iron), dark stool (from iron). Rare: allergic reactions, iron overload.
interactions: Drug interactions: Tetracycline/Fluoroquinolone antibiotics (iron and calcium reduce absorption — take 2 hours apart), Levodopa (B6 may reduce effect), Levothyroxine (take 4 hours apart). Food interactions: Best taken with a meal to improve absorption and reduce stomach upset.
contraindications: Hemochromatosis (iron overload), Wilson's disease (copper content), hypervitaminosis A or D.
storage_instructions: Store below 30°C. Keep in original container. Protect from moisture.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 1 tablet daily with a meal. Do not exceed the recommended daily dose.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Not critical — just resume the regular schedule.

name: Rabeprazole 20mg
description: A proton pump inhibitor used to treat GERD, peptic ulcers, and H. pylori eradication in combination with antibiotics. Reduces stomach acid production.
side_effects: Common: headache, diarrhea, nausea, flatulence, pharyngitis. Rare: C. difficile infection, bone fractures (long-term), magnesium deficiency, interstitial nephritis.
interactions: Drug interactions: Methotrexate (increased levels), Warfarin (monitor INR), Rilpivirine (AVOID — reduced absorption). Food interactions: Can be taken with or without food. Swallow whole — do not crush or chew.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to PPIs or substituted benzimidazoles. Concurrent use with rilpivirine.
storage_instructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from moisture. Keep in original blister packaging.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 20mg once daily. For ulcer healing: 20mg daily for 4–8 weeks. For H. pylori: 20mg twice daily with antibiotics for 7 days.
missed_dose_guidance: Take as soon as you remember. If close to next dose, skip it. Do not double dose.
